sections.h2: Harrison County and who taxes property there
sections.html:
Harrison County is in north-central West Virginia, with Clarksburg as its seat. Bridgeport, Clarksburg, Salem, Shinnston, Stonewood, Anmoore, Lumberport, Nutter Fort and West Milford are among its incorporated places, and Interstate 79 runs through the county. Four bodies bill against a Harrison County parcel: the state, the county commission, the county board of education and, inside a municipality, the city or town.

Housing demand leans on health care, federal employment and offices along I-79. United Hospital Center and the FBI's Criminal Justice Information Services Division are among the larger employers. A big employer does not fix an individual house with a failing roof or a tenant problem, though. Sellers with those issues still price against what a buyer will pay after repairs.

sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
The assessor values property and the sheriff collects the tax. Both are in the General Services Building at 229 South Third Street in Clarksburg.

QuestionPhone
Assessor's Office, general304-624-8510
Taxes due (how much you owe)304-624-8685
Homestead exemptions304-624-8540
Mobile home assessments304-624-8517
Oil and gas and minerals division304-624-8523

The assessor's site lists separate numbers for individual and business assessments as well. The office posts summer satellite days at places such as Meadowbrook Mall, the Clarksburg Senior Center and several fire stations, so people in Shinnston, Lost Creek or Spelter do not always need to drive downtown. Filing is also available online through the state's SmartFile system.

sections.h2: Filing dates and the homestead exemption
sections.html:
The assessor's 2026 filing season runs from July 1, and the dates differ by form. Individual personal property returns are due between July 1 and October 1. Business personal property returns and farm exemption applications are due between July 1 and September 1. Homestead exemption applications can be filed from July 1 through December 1 to take effect for the following tax year.

Tax tickets follow the state schedule. They go out on or after July 15, the first installment is due September 1 and the second March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount applies before those dates. Unpaid first-half tax becomes delinquent on October 1 and second-half tax on April 1, with 9 percent annual interest.

The homestead exemption removes the first $20,000 of assessed value for an owner who is 65 or older or certified permanently and totally disabled and who meets the residency rule. If you qualify, confirm the exemption was actually filed. A missed filing means a higher bill on a house you are about to sell.

Talk to the Assessor's Office first. If that does not settle it, take the dispute to the Harrison County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which meets from February 1 and finishes by February 28. The board can reduce a value that exceeds 60 percent of true and actual value, and it must give written notice at least five days before raising one.

If the board rules against you, the next step is the Office of Tax Appeals, with a petition due by March 31 of the tax year. Missing the February window waives the right to argue that year's list. A dispute over whether a home is Class II or Class IV is handled separately with the assessor and the Tax Commissioner.

Good evidence is concrete: a recent appraisal, a repair estimate for a damaged structure, or sales of similar homes. If you plan to sell soon, an appeal is often not worth the effort unless the value is clearly wrong, because the new owner will be assessed on the next cycle anyway.

sections.h2: Unpaid tax and a cash sale
sections.html:
The sheriff certifies unpaid real estate tax for sale, and the State Auditor, not the sheriff, now runs the lien sale. The certification deadline is October 31. Call the Sheriff at 304-624-8685 before you assume anything about timing or redemption cost.

A seller who owes tax can often clear it through closing. The title company obtains a payoff and pays it from the proceeds. The county excise tax on a recorded deed is 55 cents for each $500 of value under the transfer tax statute.

We buy houses in Harrison County as-is, so a house in Clarksburg that needs a roof, has a tenant, or carries back taxes does not need to be fixed first. Call or text (424) 435-2326 for a written cash offer.

sections.h2: Minerals, mobile homes and property classes
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office keeps separate divisions for mobile homes and for oil, gas and minerals. A mobile home may be assessed through its own desk at 304-624-8517, and oil and gas or mineral matters go to 304-624-8523. The state also runs its own appraisal process for oil and gas royalties.

When you sell, ask the assessor and your title company whether any mineral interest is tied to the parcel and whether it carries its own assessment. Deeds do not always say, and a buyer will want a clear answer. Cash buyers are generally fine with houses where title questions like this need work, and we check before we make an offer.

West Virginia's four classes matter too. Class II covers owner-occupied residential property used exclusively as a home. Property in a municipality that does not qualify, such as a rental house in Clarksburg, falls in Class IV, and property outside a municipality falls in Class III. Those classes have higher regular ceilings than Class II.

Before you list or accept an offer, run through a short checklist. Call 304-624-8685 for the amount due on each ticket. Ask the Assessor's Office which class the house is in and whether the homestead exemption is on file. Check whether a mobile home or mineral interest has its own assessment. Then give the title company all of it so the payoff and the deed tax are lined up before the closing date.

If the taxes are old, the house needs work, or heirs have not agreed, a sale for cash skips much of the waiting. The title company still pays what is owed from your proceeds, and you avoid repair bills and showings.

faqs.q: When are Harrison County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due September 1 and half March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay before each date. Taxes unpaid after October 1 (first half) or April 1 (second half) are delinquent and accrue 9 percent yearly interest.

faqs.q: Where is the Harrison County Sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 229 South 3rd Street, Clarksburg, WV 26301, and the phone for taxes due is 304-624-8685. Online payment is also offered.

faqs.q: When can I apply for the homestead exemption in Harrison County?
faqs.a: Eligible homeowners apply between July 1 and December 1 to receive the exemption for the following tax year. It covers the first $20,000 of assessed value for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Harrison County assessment?
faqs.a: Protest to the county commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which starts February 1 and ends by February 28. An appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals is due March 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Harrison County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A title company can get a payoff for the unpaid tax and pay it from the sale proceeds at closing.
